chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Dahqan, from Durust ibn Abu Mansur, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, a Prophet from the Prophets complained to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, about weakness and infrequent intercourse, so He commanded him to eat al-Hareesah.
ai.seo_question: What did Allah command a Prophet to eat to cure weakness and infrequent intercourse?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) relates that a Prophet complained to Allah about physical weakness and low libido, receiving a divine prescription of 'al-Hareesah' (a nutrient-rich mash of grains and meat). This narration underscores the Shia scholarly view that dietary interventions are not merely practical but divinely ordained for restoring vitality, linking physical sustenance directly to spiritual and bodily well-being.
